etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ner-bi, neer by, equivalent to near +‎ by.

definitions.definition: (finance) A futures contract, of a particular group, whose settlement date is the earliest.

quote.citation: 1984, Jack D. Schwager, A Complete Guide to the Futures Markets, page 496:
quote.text: In each of these markets the nearbys are almost invariably at a discount — a discount that tends to widen in bull markets and narrow in bear markets.

quote.citation: 1989, Raymond M. Leuthold, Joan C. Junkus, Jean E. Cordier, The Theory and Practice of Futures Markets, page 67:
quote.text: The deferred contract should be expected to rise, and buying the deferred while selling the nearby is then profitable.
